reviews.text: People who love their job and don't put people in financial difficulty, but help you in every way! Exceptional people.

My experience with SOS Veterinaria S.r.l. was profoundly negative and ended with the death of our beloved cat, Alfred.
I'd like to begin with something I hadn't verified before his admission, which I believe is important to understand. The Chamber of Commerce registration for SOS Veterinaria S.r.l. reveals a corporate structure that, in my opinion, deserves careful consideration by anyone who approaches the facility as a veterinary clinic: among the activities listed in the registration are the sale of animal feed and the rental of premises, rooms, and equipment to individual veterinarians for the practice of veterinary medicine.
Had I acquired and read that registration before entrusting Alfred to the facility, I personally wouldn't have approached his admission with the same confidence.
During his hospitalization—and here I'm referring exclusively to my own documented experience—Alfred underwent clinical procedures, some of which were highly invasive. Yet, before their execution, I was not adequately informed of the risks, potential benefits, therapeutic alternatives, and the reasons why those procedures were deemed necessary. Therefore, in my opinion, I was not allowed to make truly informed decisions about what was being done to my cat.
This is one of the aspects I consider most serious of the entire affair: when you entrust a sick animal to professionals, especially when faced with invasive procedures, you expect not only technical expertise, but also information, transparency, and the ability to understand and evaluate what is being proposed.
My mistake was not first informing myself about the precise nature of the company to which I was entrusting Alfred and not downloading the relevant company registration before he was admitted.
This is a mistake I can no longer correct.
Alfred died after being admitted and after undergoing procedures that, in light of what happened and the documentation in my possession, I continue to question whether they were all necessary and appropriate.
For me, Alfred was not "a clinical case." He was part of our family. I'm writing this review so that anyone who finds themselves in the same situation as me can do what I didn't: get informed beforehand, verify the exact person to whom they're entrusting their pet, ask who the veterinarian responsible for each clinical decision is, and demand, before any invasive procedure, clear explanations about the needs, risks, benefits, and possible alternatives.
I should have asked these questions beforehand.
Unfortunately, Alfred and those of us who loved him paid the price for that mistake.
IF YOU HAVE AN EMERGENCY, DO NOT GO HERE! The wait times are unacceptable for an emergency room. If you don't have the staff to guarantee the service you offer, I recommend you close.

Excellent expertise, kind and well-trained, excellent doctors and all the staff. I can only thank the entire staff for taking care of my feline's problem after a disastrous experience at another clinic! Highly recommended.

My cat was fine last Thursday. I took him in for a cold. They gave him antibiotics on his 15-day-old paw. On Saturday morning, my cat couldn't walk anymore. I took him to them and they did a simple x-ray of his paw (crazy). On Sunday, I came back because he wasn't breathing and had a fever. They washed their hands of it, telling me to go to another hospital. My cat is dying, and I will always regret having taken him to the wrong clinic. You can't die like this. ❤️‍🩹

I want to thank Dr. Maurelli and his team for their professionalism, preparation, dedication, and empathy during the double surgery our dog Tobia underwent. I'd especially like to emphasize their willingness to help even when complications arose that could have seriously affected our dog's health.
Thank you, thank you, thank you, thank you so much!!!!

Expert, empathetic, and very courteous staff. I thank Dr. Giovanna and dentist Dr. Daniele Calcatelli.
A clinic where care is enhanced by love and humanity.
I would like to thank all the doctors and staff at the SOS Veterinary Clinic for saving my Bull Terrier Venere. I will always be grateful to you.
Not only excellent veterinarians but also affectionate with our animal companions

I went on a Sunday because my dog ​​had a foxtail in his ear. No waiting, three super professional and kind vets. After other pretentious clinics that make you wait hours and charge through the roof, this emergency room is a real asset. You can see the true dedication here. Well done!

We brought our cat because he had been vomiting for 24 hours and was completely apathetic. When we got there, we had an abdominal ultrasound and immediately afterward, emergency surgery. The doctors performed the surgery, kept the cat hospitalized, and discharged him. The staff was very kind and professional, both the surgeon and Dr. Loffari, who after the ultrasound explained to us in detail what they were going to do and why, and of course all the nurses. Thank you so much.
Always there for the needs of our furry friends
They love animals, and I think that's more than enough. A note of praise and learning goes to the entire staff, especially Dr. Maurelli for his professionalism and humanity.
Excellent veterinary clinic

I have to compliment this clinic; my only regret is that I didn't discover it sooner. The vets are excellent and competent, but also kind and honest. Especially Dr. Virginia, who took such great care of my cat. Thank you!!!
I went just yesterday for the tests my 11-year-old Labrador needed, and they were very professional and kind, as always.
Very good doctor

What can I say... I wanted to thank them all from the bottom of my heart, an incredible team, generous, and always available, from the secretaries to all the doctors and nurses.
You saved my dog ​​and never gave up, even when I probably didn't believe it anymore.
Thank you, thank you, thank you so much!!!
Keep it up. My family, I, and my ISOTTA will thank you forever.

We brought a small dog in for a checkup due to blood in the urine. The doctor who examined her was very attentive and thorough. After administering an anti-inflammatory, she advised us to try collecting a urine sample to evaluate the treatment. The price was very fair for the treatment received. I recommend the place to anyone who needs it.

Unfortunately, I can't give it less than one star.

I've tried to contact them several times, as they're the closest 24-hour clinic to my home, and I've had terrible experiences every time.

My dog ​​was admitted to their clinic, and I could only see him at certain times, as if we were in the hospital, which didn't fit with my work schedule. I basically couldn't see him, nor could I speak to the doctors to find out how he was, terrified of seeing him leave the clinic without being alive (having no way to see him or find out how he was).

Two years ago, I brought my cat in around 11 PM with severe kidney failure. They diagnosed him and told me it was urgent to intervene immediately, but there was nothing they could do. Aren't you a 24-hour clinic?!? Can't you even perform a catheter, empty his bladder, and hospitalize him?! I had to rush to another 24-hour clinic (Clinica Etiopia, which I highly recommend), risking the cat dying on the way there!

But the icing on the cake was when a young lady at the register, not to resort to any other terminology, dared to judge me in front of other people in the waiting room for the fact that I shouldn't have had a dog and a cat, aged 14 and 4, respectively, while also having a baby of just a few months, because I should have imagined there would be financial costs involved. I had simply asked if they offered installment payments via SumUp (which other vets do).

You're inhumane, that's all I can say, reading about other people's experiences besides my own...

The best 24-hour emergency room in the capital. Dr. Mezzanotte, the emergency room manager, is without a doubt
the most competent doctor I've ever met. I owe the lives of my five pets to her and the staff. Thank you so much.

A highly respectable clinic. My puppies had surgeries with Dr. Maurelli, who proved to be empathetic and of a high standard, with exceptional results. Dr. Giovanna, of course, was always present and attentive to any needs.
I can't give more than 5 stars because it's not expected.
Top-notch staff
Thank you again 😍😍😍

I've been coming to this clinic for 30 years, having had a dog for 14 years and now a 16-year-old. I've always been happy with various issues related to thyroidism, arthritis, asthma, liver cancer, and various cysts for both dogs. Orthopedics: Dr. Carlo Maurelli; Dermatology, Endocrinology and Other: Dr. Giovanna Cacciutto; Dental Care: Dr. Daniele Calcatelli; Ultrasound: Dr. Roberto Loffari; Anesthesiologists: Dr. Mezzanotte and Dr. Marco
Everyone has contributed and continues to contribute to the health of my dogs. Professional and helpful.

Absolutely avoid! I took my dog ​​here for a tail problem, they couldn't muzzle him or examine him, and in the chaos, while I was trying to muzzle him, the "doctor" gave her diagnosis (I don't know how she did it) for €90 without having done anything to him! Scandalous and thieving! I advise against going to this clinic!

I'm giving one star because it's impossible to give less. The doctor who was on duty as an anesthesiologist on Saturday, December 13th, without even introducing herself, lacking clarity, kindness, or humanity, and above all, lacking the slightest knowledge of a seriously ill, chronically ill patient with multiple problems, including epilepsy, suggested immediate surgery, trying to make me feel guilty about my questions and reluctance, as if I weren't a good owner. Indeed, she threatened me with terrifying prospects if I didn't. She treated us with absolute superficiality and arrogance. I went there because another specialist recommended it for an emergency x-ray. Honestly, I'd had negative experiences there in the past and was hoping to change my mind. Since my dog ​​got sick, a year ago, I've been to clinics, undergone practically every type of therapy and test, and never before had anyone treated us like this. I had a terrible experience with this doctor. I might also add that the reception was run-down. The welcome was zero.

I brought an unhealthy adopted kitten to my first visit with Dr. Cacciutto. She was exceptional, highly knowledgeable, and patiently and kindly explained all the treatments to me. The ladies at reception were also excellent, attentive and very kind to the owners and the animals. I've been going there for 40 years and, after six dogs and four cats of all breeds and with all sorts of problems, they remain a center of excellence and expertise, and I would recommend them for any need. I'm attaching photos of some of my own animals, all cared for by them.

Absolutely to be avoided, cynical and disorganized. I brought my dog ​​that was hit by a car, they operated on her, and she came home paralyzed without being informed of what could happen. I had to call after two weeks to find out if she needed to be checked and if she needed to have her stitches removed, and they said yes, ma'am. But shouldn't they have told me this when I was discharged instead of just giving me the bill for several euros? Over 2000?

My dog ​​was hospitalized for 17 days; he was 16 years old and in critical condition. They did everything they could to save him and heal him, with unparalleled skill and sensitivity. Everyone—vets, nurses, and administrative staff—were gentle, helpful, and available for every need. And it was my first time there. My dog ​​was taken care of in the best possible way.
They're the absolute worst. Avoid them! My dog ​​died because of them. They're only interested in money. I know dozens of people who've lost their pets because of them.
Arrived at 8am, no emergency doctor, congratulations, change the name of the clinic

Given all the negative posts, I'd really like to join in with everyone who's had a harrowing experience in this hole, a dirty one if I remember correctly.
Perhaps I should have written this review sooner, since I'm talking about a case from a few years ago.
I took my poor SMALL mixed-breed dog to the house in the middle of the night, and I still have the face of the BRAT—sorry for the term—who was pretending to be a doctor.
They tried to take an X-ray on my dog, telling me that if he got agitated, they'd have to muzzle him and that I'd have to hold him down anyway.
My furry friend was 20 years old at the time, with rheumatics and loose teeth—you can imagine—even bathing him, poor thing, was difficult. If we did, he'd stay still for days. Imagine how aggressive he could be. In any case, I held him down, scared, and it brought back heartbreaking memories.
90 euros for telling me nothing, and not only that, they give me a stomach ache that I had to put in my dog's mouth myself because the brat was probably disgusted.
Zero tact, zero enthusiasm, zero love, zero professionalism.
At the time, I left mortified, but today... I'll leave you to draw your own conclusions.
I strongly urge you not to take your friends there, because apparently nothing has changed in all these years.
Luckily, some time later, I took my dog ​​to the vets at Villa Bonelli. They're good, patient, generous, honest, and above all, they don't just see profit in what they do, quite the opposite.
So, thank you to Luca and Fabio for allowing my poor puppy to choose to leave with peace of mind and, above all, DIGNITY!

No.
I won't be returning to this clinic.
Hovel of a stay, unhelpful, rude staff, and, of course, completely unsympathetic.

They never answer the phone, and if you insist, they hang up on you!!!!
After surgery, the wound reopened 20 days later, and they don't give you an explanation or how to proceed.
My cat may die, but I put her through 11 days of hell. I took her away because they said she wasn't responding to the medications or eating. But at home, it only took two days for her to regain weight and feel calm. The medications did their job.
My cat may die (I still haven't had the histology report after 20 days), but I think it's pretty advanced, but I won't be setting foot in there again.
I hadn't read the reviews, otherwise I would have gone elsewhere, since the prices are definitely high.
Zerostelle

A horrific and traumatic experience at the clinic... we took our beautiful dog, not even 4 years old, for a simple foxtail in his nose. He was given general anesthesia, and for some unknown reason, he went into cardiac arrest and died.
So draw your own conclusions about the clinic.
We went in with a young, healthy dog ​​and left with a dead dog with no valid explanation, and so we are desperate.

I cannot judge medical expertise because I decided to take my cat away due to the very obvious weaknesses of the staff I dealt with. Much work needs to be done to achieve a more humane approach to welcoming and communicating, and, in one case, even basic courtesy. Without wanting or being able to discuss strictly medical aspects, I feel I must say that without a little empathy and courtesy, professional knowledge is insufficient.

Our cat was special, he was part of our family. We trusted him. We paid for a hospital stay that lasted too long without anything being done for him. Left without food, in our opinion, because there was no doctor to take care of him during a cursed long weekend. We trusted him and we will never forgive ourselves. It won't help bring him back, but I hope it will help make us think.
Very good and professional

I can't speak for the entire staff because I don't know them, but yesterday during the ultrasound, the doctor gave me a harsh verdict without a shred of empathy or tact.
With the same coldness, he outlined the fee schedule for any subsequent actions to be taken.
You may have made the best diagnosis in the world, dear doctor, but your methods need to be completely reconsidered.
It's never too late to learn.
Absolutely not recommended, I had a sad and bad experience with my dog.

My dog ​​Trilly is being treated at the clinic...unfortunately he suffers from a serious disease that has affected the spleen and liver...every time I have had to resort to them, even in the evening hours, I have always found competent people who assisted me. Now the oncologist Dr. Giovanna has recommended palliative care and my dog ​​is back to eating and shows no suffering...thank you 🙏
Not recommended!! Poor professionalism and total disorganization!

HORRIBLE EXPERIENCE...7 different diagnoses...and possibly surgery...by a professional...the dog has nothing wrong, not even the inflammatory phase...just changed the food...because of the heat and had an ultrasound...NOTHING AT ALL
NEVER AGAIN ZERO STARS

Thanks to Doctor Maurelli and his team, all included, for the kindness and professionalism of the work they do with passion and patience towards our puppies, the Doctor sterilized my dog ​​... TOP, and also took care of another problem that did not concern the surgery always on the same day ... and which we are solving, thank you so much

Thanks to S.o.s. Veterinaria, especially to Dr. Giovanna, who accompanied my beloved Haigor into his new life today with infinite care and kindness.
Thanks also to Anna Maria and all the staff.

I turned to SOS Veterinary in an emergency situation. My cat Nina was hospitalized at the clinic for several days, during which she was cared for by the entire staff with great professionalism, attention, and love. Despite the sad outcome, unfortunately due to the incurability of her case, my daughter and I extend our heartfelt thanks to all the staff for their honesty, sensitivity, and support until the very end.

I took my cat to the vet with blood on his face and he couldn't eat. They immediately took matters into their own hands, saying that if he hissed, they wouldn't check him (shouldn't a vet be able to handle a hissing cat?). It's natural for an older cat to be a little nervous at the vet, but he didn't even try to scratch the poor thing. Anyway, in the end, I kept him there, and with my cell phone flashlight (which seems unprofessional to me), they could see that his gums were swollen, without being able to determine whether or not he had an infection. They even told me "he might have a tumor." Fortunately, I'm a rational person with experience with both cats and dogs, so I wasn't alarmed. In fact, today my trusted vet told me it was just inflammation, treatable with a soothing gel and an anti-inflammatory (which they didn't even prescribe at the emergency room).
I also had an unpleasant experience in 2007 when I took my Beagle puppy to the vet several times; They couldn't recognize Ehrlichiosis, a deadly disease.
I hoped that after all these years, things had improved.
On holidays, when we can't take our pets to the trusted vet, we should be able to count on these facilities...

A horrible experience.

My dog, Lilly, unfortunately had a serious illness, and instead of helping us through this time, they made it even darker and more stressful.

They never answered my phone or texts.
She had been placed in a room where she couldn't get up because she kept slipping, and the room wasn't up to safety standards.
The doctor wasn't fully informed about her condition.
Huge blisters had appeared on Lilly's body, and every time I asked the doctor about it, she told me that wasn't the most important thing, without ever giving me an answer.

My dog ​​had never been alone, and she was definitely scared in that place. After I told the doctor that letting her stay with her family might make her feel more at ease, since in the previous days she had only been able to eat and walk with us (when we were allowed to meet her) and not with them, she still shushed me and told me it wasn't true.

The impression I got when I took Lilly away was that they purposely wanted us to feel like we were doing the wrong thing and that they were the only ones worried about her. For more than five days, they never once cared about her condition.

Unfortunately, Lilly had an incurable disease, and for us owners, losing a friend is always heartbreaking. I know I gave her all the love in the world, and honestly, the only thing I regret is having entrusted her to "professionals" like them.

Change jobs. My cat's bladder had to be punctured to insert a catheter, and luckily I saved him by taking him to another clinic, which was able to confirm the situation with an ultrasound and operate immediately. Never see you again.

I went on Sunday for my Labrador who had a bad case of gastroenteritis. She received a very thorough examination, and the doctors took exceptional care of her. Very fair prices, and the staff were very kind and professional.

Unfriendly doctors to say the least, yesterday I brought my dog ​​and the doctor wouldn't even let me speak, I was in the veterinary emergency room, she looked at me really badly. The diagnosis was not made, only a piece of chewed hand was …
Inefficient, unavailable and incompetent.
Incompetent and not very sensitive.

Unfortunately, we were forced to give 1 star.
On Sunday afternoon, we were greeted with a "wait and see," as if they were trying to send us away. Furthermore, the cat (with a cut on its rubber band), after …
Useless ungrateful people service business purpose

In the midst of an emergency, it was closed. Obviously, it wasn't listed on the website that said it was open. A wasted trip.
The 24-hour service is specifically for emergencies when vets are closed. Thank you very much.
